actions.label: Allow FWB and its local assistants to manage distribution, with guards providing security only
Let guard and militia structures carry out distribution
Grant FWB staff unrestricted freedom of movement in the camp
Press ministries for rations, guard pay and infrastructure funding
Permit an escorted FWB nutritional assessment
Provide ongoing food aid deliveries to the camp
Consult refugees on their needs during distribution
Provide food rations to guards and their families
Extend food support to affected host-community households
Follow the camp's MASHA-style access process via Camp Admin
Accept a joint distribution by guards and FWB staff, monitored by FWB
Have guards carry out distribution block by block, pausing a block if trouble occurs

goals.label: FWB staff move freely inside the camp
Ongoing food aid supply reaches the camp
Camp commander and guards control food distribution and camp operations
Camp obtains government rations and funding
Camp power and infrastructure keep functioning
Commander's authority with guards is preserved or he appears weak
Commander's standing with the Senior Militia Leader and personal safety
FWB controls food distribution and who carries it out
FWB staff and local assistants are safe
FWB's neutrality and independence are preserved
Food aid is diverted to guards and militia
Food is distributed without excluding or discriminating against refugee groups
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Host town economy and goodwill are protected
Hostile actors or terrorists exploit outsider access to harm the camp
Refugees have a voice in the aid they receive
Refugees receive the food intended for them in adequate quantity
Refugees stay contained in the camp and away from the capital
Refugees' nutritional needs are assessed and documented for donor accountability
Resource-heavy procedures like nutritional assessments are imposed on the camp
Existing relationship with MASHA is maintained
FWB's reputation and visibility with donors and public

redLines.label: Stop diverting food to guards and deliver full rations to all registered refugees
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head.

redLines.label: Approve hiring of local host-town workers for FWB activities
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Hire and source locally from the host community

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
